# llm-cache-proxy

Zero-dependency local Messages replay proxy. [src: README.md]
Validate offline: `npm run validate`. [src: package.json]
Start: `./cachectl-a.sh setup` then `./cachectl-a.sh on`. [src: USAGE.md]
Paid opt-ins: `npm run test:fidelity`, `python3 bench.py`. [src: package.json; bench.py]
Read `docs/wiki/README.md` for maintained references. [src: docs/wiki/README.md]

## Source: README.md [src: README.md]

# llm-cache-proxy [src: README.md]

A local, zero-dependency reverse proxy for the Anthropic Messages API. Repeated [src: README.md]
requests replay the stored response bytes without another upstream call. It fits [src: README.md]
reruns, evaluations, CI and scripted development loops. New prompts still cost a [src: README.md]
normal API call; normalization and suffix matching are explicit opt-ins. [src: README.md]

## Quick start [src: README.md]

Use Node 18 or newer to run the tools; use Node 22 or newer for coverage checks. [src: README.md]

```bash
git clone https://github.com/mithudso/llm-cache-proxy.git
cd llm-cache-proxy
./cachectl-a.sh setup
./cachectl-a.sh on
export ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:4000
export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=anything
```

Setup stores your real key in the ignored `.env`. For an installed npm or Homebrew [src: README.md]
package, use `llm-cache-proxy setup` and `llm-cache-proxy on`; its config lives in [src: README.md]
`~/.llm-cache-a/.env`. See [installation](docs/INSTALLATION.md). [src: README.md]

## Behavior [src: README.md]

- Byte-exact JSON and SSE replay, including tool-use responses. [src: README.md]
- Complete successful responses only; interrupted streams never become hits. [src: README.md]
- Request coalescing, async cache I/O, TTL and LRU eviction. [src: README.md]
- Loopback by default; a non-loopback bind requires `CACHE_AUTH_TOKEN`. [src: README.md]
- Session and all-time statistics, Prometheus metrics and a live SSE monitor. [src: README.md]
- Optional normalized and suffix keys; suffix mode can return out-of-context data. [src: README.md]
- An installed Node CLI, source Bash controller and cache explorer. [src: README.md]

The proxy (`proxy-a.mjs`) forwards a cache miss to `api.anthropic.com`, streams the [src: README.md]
response to the client and writes a private local cache entry. Exact cache identity [src: README.md]
includes the body and relevant HTTP context. [Architecture](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md) [src: README.md]
explains identity, coalescing and storage. [src: README.md]

## Operate and develop [src: README.md]

```bash
./cachectl-a.sh validate
./cachectl-a.sh status
./cachectl-a.sh stats
./cachectl-a.sh monitor
./cachectl-a.sh explore --list
./cachectl-a.sh off       # bypass mode; still forwards paid requests
./cachectl-a.sh stop
npm run validate         # offline mock tests, syntax and documentation checks
```

`npm run test:fidelity` and `python3 bench.py` make live, paid requests. Run them [src: README.md]
only deliberately. Built-in dollar rates are estimates; check the provider invoice. [src: README.md]

Start with the maintained [project wiki](docs/wiki/README.md), [usage guide](USAGE.md), [src: README.md]
[development guide](docs/DEVELOPMENT.md), [test strategy](docs/TESTING.md), [src: README.md]
[security model](docs/SECURITY.md) and [contributing guide](CONTRIBUTING.md). [src: README.md]
The [bootstrap audit](docs/repo-bootstrap-audit-2026-11-12.md) records adaptations [src: README.md]
and the [optimizer report](docs/code-deep-optimizer-2026-11-12.md) records verification. [src: README.md]
Licensed under [MIT](LICENSE). [src: README.md]


## Source: USAGE.md [src: USAGE.md]

# Usage guide [src: USAGE.md]

## Controllers [src: USAGE.md]

The installed `llm-cache-proxy` command (`cli.mjs`) supports `on`, `off`, `restart`, [src: USAGE.md]
`stop`, `stats`, `setup` and `validate`. With no command it prints help. [src: USAGE.md]

The source `./cachectl-a.sh` supports those commands plus `status`, `monitor`, [src: USAGE.md]
`explore`, `run`, `install`, `uninstall` and `--help`. [src: USAGE.md]
`off` starts bypass mode: requests still go upstream and incur cost. [src: USAGE.md]
`stop` stops the owned instance. Service install/uninstall changes user services. [src: USAGE.md]
Both controllers verify PID identity before signaling a process. [src: USAGE.md]

Use `127.0.0.1` for the default IPv4 bind. For an IPv6 bind, use `[::1]` in URLs. [src: USAGE.md]
Source config comes from `<repo>/.env`; installed config comes from [src: USAGE.md]
`~/.llm-cache-a/.env`, with `./.env` as fallback. Config is parsed as data. [src: USAGE.md]
Shell code and command substitution in `.env` are never executed. [src: USAGE.md]

## HTTP endpoints [src: USAGE.md]

| Method | Path | Result | [src: USAGE.md]
|---|---|---| [src: USAGE.md]
| POST | `/v1/messages` | MISS forwards; HIT replays bytes | [src: USAGE.md]
| GET | `/health` | Open liveness probe | [src: USAGE.md]
| GET | `/stats` | All-time counters and nested `.session` counters | [src: USAGE.md]
| GET | `/metrics` | Prometheus text | [src: USAGE.md]
| GET | `/monitor` | Live SSE events; may contain response snippets | [src: USAGE.md]

When configured, send `x-cache-auth: <token>` to every endpoint except `/health`. [src: USAGE.md]
`x-cache-bypass: 1` disables caching for a request. `x-cache` identifies `MISS`, [src: USAGE.md]
`HIT`, `HIT-NORM`, `HIT-SUFFIX`, `HIT-COALESCED`, `MISS-COALESCED` or `ERROR`. [src: USAGE.md]
A successful liveness probe does not prove an API key works upstream. [src: USAGE.md]

## Cache inspection [src: USAGE.md]

```bash
node cache-explorer.mjs --list
node cache-explorer.mjs --json
node cache-explorer.mjs --view abcd
node cache-explorer.mjs --invalidate abcd
```

Use a hexadecimal prefix of 4–64 characters. Viewing requires one match; [src: USAGE.md]
invalidation deletes all matches. The interactive TUI supports arrows or j/k, [src: USAGE.md]
Enter, d/x to invalidate, r to refresh, and q/Ctrl-C to exit. Human displays escape [src: USAGE.md]
terminal controls; JSON output remains machine-readable. Cache bodies can contain [src: USAGE.md]
private response text. Keep exported JSON and inspected bodies private. [src: USAGE.md]

## Partial matching [src: USAGE.md]

Copy `normalize.json.example` to `~/.llm-cache-a/normalize.json`, review the patterns, [src: USAGE.md]
run `./cachectl-a.sh validate`, then restart deliberately. [src: USAGE.md]
`system_strip` and `message_strip` are arrays of JavaScript regex strings applied [src: USAGE.md]
to string system/message content. Matches become `<NORM>`. Structured content blocks [src: USAGE.md]
are preserved. `suffix_only` defaults false; `suffix_turns` defaults to 3 and must [src: USAGE.md]
be a positive integer. Suffix matching ignores earlier messages and may serve an [src: USAGE.md]
answer from a different conversation. Patterns can also merge semantically distinct [src: USAGE.md]
requests. Use only when your workload justifies these equivalences. [src: USAGE.md]

## Configuration and paths [src: USAGE.md]

[Development](docs/DEVELOPMENT.md) lists every environment variable. [src: USAGE.md]
[Architecture](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md) explains storage and key identity. [src: USAGE.md]
[Installation](docs/INSTALLATION.md) covers services, upgrades and removal. [src: USAGE.md]
[Runbooks](docs/runbooks/operations.md) cover diagnosis and recovery. [src: USAGE.md]


## Source: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md [src: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md]

# Architecture [src: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md]

## Context and containers [src: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md]

```text
Client (Messages API)
        | HTTP + optional x-cache-auth
        v
Local Node proxy ---- MISS / real key ----> Anthropic HTTPS
        |
        +---- complete bounded response ----> private filesystem cache
        +---- outcome ----------------------> metrics ledger + local logs
        +---- live event -------------------> authenticated monitor clients

Node CLI / Bash controller --> owned proxy process + read-only health probes
Cache explorer            --> local cache files (explicit invalidation)
```

This is one Node ESM package without runtime npm dependencies. `proxy-a.mjs` owns [src: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md]
HTTP forwarding, caching and monitoring. `lib/proxy-config.mjs` captures validated [src: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md]
limits from `lib/proxy-validation.mjs`. Controllers share `lib/controller.mjs` for [src: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md]
safe configuration, bounded probes and process identity. The independent explorer [src: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md]
reads the same store. The benchmark uses Python's standard library. [src: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md]

## Request flow and identity [src: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md]

1. Match supported endpoints and authenticate all except exact `GET /health`. [src: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md]
2. Read a bounded Messages request and validate usable model/body shape. [src: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md]
3. Hash model, raw body and API context. Query strings and response-affecting [src: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md]
   Anthropic headers partition exact, normalized, suffix and inflight keys. [src: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md]
4. Try exact disk hit, then opt-in normalized/suffix aliases. Check TTL and any [src: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md]
   stored body digest before replaying bytes. [src: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md]
5. Join an identical in-flight operation or forward one upstream request. [src: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md]
6. Stream with backpressure, enforce a deadline, and settle aborted operations. [src: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md]
7. Publish a complete bounded 200 response, record actual persistence and outcome. [src: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md]

The legacy default key is `sha256(model + "\\n" + raw body)` when the default path [src: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md]
has no additional API context. Header/query context produces a separate namespace. [src: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md]
`node proxy-a.mjs key <model> <body>` computes the legacy default key only. [src: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md]
Normalization substitutes selected string fields. Suffix mode also drops earlier [src: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md]
messages; both deliberately weaken semantic identity and remain opt-in. [src: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md]

A stream requires a terminal SSE event frame rather than a substring in response [src: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md]
text. A truncated or oversized response cannot be a reusable hit. Oversized bodies [src: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md]
continue streaming to the primary client; waiters can fall back to their own fetch. [src: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md]
The primary client's abort cancels its upstream request; waiters can then retry [src: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md]
through their own fetch path. No blanket automatic paid retry policy is introduced. [src: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md]

## Storage and deployment [src: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md]

`~/.llm-cache-a/entries/<key>.bin` holds raw bytes; `.json` holds timestamp, content [src: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md]
type, optional content encoding, model, usage and, for new entries, body hash. Temporary files and rename prevent [src: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md]
partial individual-file publication; a digest rejects mismatched pairs. A mismatch [src: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md]
can cause a safe miss during concurrent alias writes. Legacy pairs remain readable. [src: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md]
New directories/files use restrictive permissions. Existing historical files are [src: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md]
not recursively rewritten. TTL checks reads; LRU uses payload mtime and entry count. [src: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md]

The proxy listens on `127.0.0.1:4000` by default. It does not bind dual-stack by [src: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md]
default. A non-loopback host requires a shared token, and the listening socket is [src: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md]
HTTP. User services are explicit source-controller operations. No deployment or [src: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md]
service activation occurs as a side effect of repository maintenance. [src: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md]

## Decisions and constraints [src: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md]

- Keep Node built-ins rather than restoring the removed LiteLLM runtime. The historical [src: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md]
  evaluation reported slow/flaky startup and no passthrough cache hits; those figures [src: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md]
  are historical evidence, not measurements of this version. [src: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md]
- Keep byte-exact replay and explicit optional equivalences rather than semantic matching. [src: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md]
- Do not retry paid operations automatically or add dashboards/databases just for audit [src: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md]
  symmetry. The local CLI, metrics and monitor are the operational surface. [src: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md]
- Keep numeric coverage gates alongside behavioral boundary tests; 100% reported lines [src: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md]
  alone did not prove header identity, stream completion or safe process control. [src: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md]

See [security](SECURITY.md), [known limits](known-issues.md), [logging](logging.md) [src: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md]
and [library APIs](COMPONENTS.md). Current live fidelity, performance, service reboots [src: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md]
and native Windows acceptance require separate validation. [src: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md]


## Source: docs/DEVELOPMENT.md [src: docs/DEVELOPMENT.md]

# Development [src: docs/DEVELOPMENT.md]

## Setup and workflow [src: docs/DEVELOPMENT.md]

Use the Node version in `.nvmrc` (22) for coverage and Python 3 for benchmark tests. [src: docs/DEVELOPMENT.md]
Runtime tools require Node 18+ and built-ins only; no npm install is needed to run [src: docs/DEVELOPMENT.md]
source tests. `npm ci --ignore-scripts` verifies the empty dependency lockfile. [src: docs/DEVELOPMENT.md]
Bash and curl are needed for the source controller. There is no bundler, build, [src: docs/DEVELOPMENT.md]
watch server or TypeScript compilation step. Edit modules and restart only your [src: docs/DEVELOPMENT.md]
own disposable development instance when needed. [src: docs/DEVELOPMENT.md]

```bash
npm run validate
node --test proxy.test.mjs
npm run docs:generate
npm run ops:doc
npm run docs:check
npm run ops:doc:check
```

Add behavior through the owning module and a test using `test-helpers.mjs` or a [src: docs/DEVELOPMENT.md]
temporary controller fixture. First reproduce the bug, then implement and run the [src: docs/DEVELOPMENT.md]
owning suite and complete gate. Keep credentials and live cache data out of fixtures. [src: docs/DEVELOPMENT.md]
Tests run in separate processes; avoid adding shared disk or fixed-port dependencies. [src: docs/DEVELOPMENT.md]

Use a focused task branch and descriptive commit. Review the final diff, push the PR, [src: docs/DEVELOPMENT.md]
wait for required checks and merge. CI runs offline tests and doc drift checks on PRs [src: docs/DEVELOPMENT.md]
and pushes. Tags may publish npm; published releases may update Homebrew. No release [src: docs/DEVELOPMENT.md]
is created by an ordinary merge. Live paid tests are manual only. [src: docs/DEVELOPMENT.md]

## Environment variables [src: docs/DEVELOPMENT.md]

Values in `.env.example` are placeholders; do not copy a real key into documentation. [src: docs/DEVELOPMENT.md]

| Variable | Default | Meaning | [src: docs/DEVELOPMENT.md]
|---|---|---| [src: docs/DEVELOPMENT.md]
| ANTHROPIC_API_KEY_REAL | required for server | Real upstream credential | [src: docs/DEVELOPMENT.md]
| CACHE_PORT | 4000 | Listen port; tests may inject ephemeral port through start(0) | [src: docs/DEVELOPMENT.md]
| CACHE_HOST | 127.0.0.1 | Bind host; non-loopback requires token | [src: docs/DEVELOPMENT.md]
| CACHE_AUTH_TOKEN | unset | Proxy authentication header value | [src: docs/DEVELOPMENT.md]
| CACHE_OFF | unset | 1 bypasses caching | [src: docs/DEVELOPMENT.md]
| CACHE_TTL_SEC | 604800 | Entry lifetime in seconds | [src: docs/DEVELOPMENT.md]
| CACHE_MAX_ENTRIES | 5000 | Maximum cache entries, including aliases | [src: docs/DEVELOPMENT.md]
| CACHE_LOG_LEVEL | info | silent, error, info or debug | [src: docs/DEVELOPMENT.md]
| CACHE_QUIET | unset | 1 is silent unless explicit log level takes precedence | [src: docs/DEVELOPMENT.md]
| CACHE_LOG_FILE | ~/.llm-cache-a/proxy.log | Additional file sink; none disables | [src: docs/DEVELOPMENT.md]
| CACHE_UPSTREAM_HOST | api.anthropic.com | Test/upstream override; no secret in value | [src: docs/DEVELOPMENT.md]
| CACHE_UPSTREAM_PORT | 443 | Upstream TCP port | [src: docs/DEVELOPMENT.md]
| CACHE_UPSTREAM_PROTO | https | http only for trusted local mocks | [src: docs/DEVELOPMENT.md]
| CACHE_MAX_REQUEST_BYTES | 33554432 | Maximum buffered request body | [src: docs/DEVELOPMENT.md]
| CACHE_MAX_RESPONSE_BYTES | 33554432 | Maximum retained response for cache/coalescing | [src: docs/DEVELOPMENT.md]
| CACHE_UPSTREAM_TIMEOUT_MS | 120000 | Upstream total request deadline | [src: docs/DEVELOPMENT.md]
| CACHE_MAX_MONITORS | 100 | Concurrent monitor connections | [src: docs/DEVELOPMENT.md]
| CACHE_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS | 2000 | Controller HTTP probe deadline | [src: docs/DEVELOPMENT.md]

The Node CLI preserves already-set environment values. Source-controller parsing [src: docs/DEVELOPMENT.md]
behavior is documented in the controller source. Configuration is read at startup. [src: docs/DEVELOPMENT.md]
`normalize.json` and `prices.json` live under `~/.llm-cache-a/`. [src: docs/DEVELOPMENT.md]
Prices map model substrings to nonnegative finite input/output dollars per token. [src: docs/DEVELOPMENT.md]
The longest matching substring wins, so a full model override beats a family rate. [src: docs/DEVELOPMENT.md]

## Troubleshooting [src: docs/DEVELOPMENT.md]

A test affected by exported CACHE_* variables needs harness isolation. Never fix it [src: docs/DEVELOPMENT.md]
by pointing tests at production. A 401 on local probes requires the same auth token. [src: docs/DEVELOPMENT.md]
Use 127.0.0.1 for IPv4 and ::1 for IPv6. An occupied port may belong to another app; [src: docs/DEVELOPMENT.md]
inspect ownership before changing it. See [runbooks](runbooks/operations.md). [src: docs/DEVELOPMENT.md]


## Source: docs/TESTING.md [src: docs/TESTING.md]

# Test strategy [src: docs/TESTING.md]

## Offline suites [src: docs/TESTING.md]

| Command | Scope | [src: docs/TESTING.md]
|---|---| [src: docs/TESTING.md]
| npm run check | Syntax of all tracked/new source modules, Bash and Python | [src: docs/TESTING.md]
| npm test | All *.test.mjs in isolated Node test processes; mock upstreams and temp homes | [src: docs/TESTING.md]
| npm run test:normalize-example | Example patterns, no real upstream | [src: docs/TESTING.md]
| npm run test:python | Benchmark cost classification and raw HTTP against a local fixture | [src: docs/TESTING.md]
| npm run docs:check | Deterministic indexes and local Markdown paths | [src: docs/TESTING.md]
| npm run ops:doc:check | Generated operations and route inventory drift | [src: docs/TESTING.md]
| npm run validate | Combined offline gate | [src: docs/TESTING.md]

Use `node --test <file>.test.mjs` for a focused run. The proxy harness imports after [src: docs/TESTING.md]
setting a temporary home, synthetic key and mock endpoint. Each file boots one proxy [src: docs/TESTING.md]
and tears down connections and files. Controller tests copy only owned scripts into [src: docs/TESTING.md]
disposable fixtures; signals never target the live installation. [src: docs/TESTING.md]

## Coverage policy [src: docs/TESTING.md]

Important and changed paths need assertions on bytes, headers, upstream call counts, [src: docs/TESTING.md]
error termination, file permissions and logs. The CI gate enforces 95% lines, 95% [src: docs/TESTING.md]
functions and 90% branches for `proxy-a.mjs`. The former blanket 100% gate excluded [src: docs/TESTING.md]
many defensive paths while missing trust-boundary defects. The new gate keeps a [src: docs/TESTING.md]
numeric regression floor while allowing real defensive branches; no new coverage [src: docs/TESTING.md]
exclusions should be added to hide failures. Helpers/controllers also receive [src: docs/TESTING.md]
behavior tests, although their coverage is not part of that numeric gate. [src: docs/TESTING.md]

Node 22+ supplies the coverage flags. CI checks Node 22 and 24; runtime remains Node [src: docs/TESTING.md]
18-compatible. A separate legacy-runtime smoke run exercises the suite without [src: docs/TESTING.md]
coverage flags. Concurrency between files is safe because each uses temporary homes [src: docs/TESTING.md]
and ephemeral ports. Disk-HIT assertions poll for metadata publication. Short observation windows remain [src: docs/TESTING.md]
for negative asynchronous assertions; avoid longer arbitrary sleeps in new tests. [src: docs/TESTING.md]

## Paid/manual tests [src: docs/TESTING.md]

`npm run test:fidelity` uses a running proxy and real Anthropic key. It checks live [src: docs/TESTING.md]
SSE/tool-use fidelity and coalescing. `python3 bench.py` sends paid misses and reports [src: docs/TESTING.md]
cache classification and estimated dollar savings. Neither runs automatically in CI. [src: docs/TESTING.md]
No live proof, reboot acceptance, native Windows service acceptance or performance [src: docs/TESTING.md]
improvement is established by the offline suite. [src: docs/TESTING.md]


## Source: docs/SECURITY.md [src: docs/SECURITY.md]

# Security model [src: docs/SECURITY.md]

## Boundaries and principals [src: docs/SECURITY.md]

The operator owns a local process, real Anthropic key and plaintext cache. A client [src: docs/SECURITY.md]
that reaches `/v1/messages` can spend that key. The proxy binds loopback by default; [src: docs/SECURITY.md]
non-loopback exposure requires a shared `CACHE_AUTH_TOKEN`. This is a local operator [src: docs/SECURITY.md]
tool, not a tenant-isolated gateway. It does not provide TLS on its listening socket. [src: docs/SECURITY.md]

## Threat model [src: docs/SECURITY.md]

| Threat | Mitigation / limit | [src: docs/SECURITY.md]
|---|---| [src: docs/SECURITY.md]
| Spoofing | Shared x-cache-auth on all routes except exact /health; loopback default | [src: docs/SECURITY.md]
| Tampering | API-context cache identity, complete-stream checks, validated config and coherent cache reads | [src: docs/SECURITY.md]
| Repudiation | Request outcomes and metrics ledger; no tamper-proof audit trail | [src: docs/SECURITY.md]
| Information disclosure | New cache files private; real key replaces client auth; local control headers stripped | [src: docs/SECURITY.md]
| Denial of service | Request/retained-response bounds, deadlines, backpressure and monitor limits | [src: docs/SECURITY.md]
| Elevation of privilege | Config parsed as data; positive PID and matching command required before signals | [src: docs/SECURITY.md]

Setup writes config privately. Do not follow config-file symlinks. Existing legacy [src: docs/SECURITY.md]
cache files may have older permissions; review them privately before reuse. Cached [src: docs/SECURITY.md]
response bodies and `/monitor` snippets can contain private text. The cache and ledger [src: docs/SECURITY.md]
are unencrypted; filesystem access is the security boundary. There is no compliance [src: docs/SECURITY.md]
attestation, customer-data isolation or encryption-at-rest claim. [src: docs/SECURITY.md]

## Contributor and incident guidance [src: docs/SECURITY.md]

Never commit real credentials, local cache bodies, transcripts or customer exports. [src: docs/SECURITY.md]
Use synthetic markers in tests. Validate headers, input shapes and log contents. [src: docs/SECURITY.md]
Do not print keys while diagnosing configuration; use presence-only status. [src: docs/SECURITY.md]
Rotate compromised keys at the provider and update local config deliberately. [src: docs/SECURITY.md]
Stop only the verified owned instance. Review logs locally; do not paste private [src: docs/SECURITY.md]
response snippets into public issues. See [reporting](../.github/SECURITY.md). [src: docs/SECURITY.md]


## Source: docs/known-issues.md [src: docs/known-issues.md]

# Known limits [src: docs/known-issues.md]

- Metrics ledger is append-only and loaded at startup; large history increases startup [src: docs/known-issues.md]
  memory/time. Preserve accounting history before any manual archival. [src: docs/known-issues.md]
- Entry count includes normalized/suffix aliases; this is not a byte quota. Expired [src: docs/known-issues.md]
  files remain until eviction or explicit invalidation. [src: docs/known-issues.md]
- Normalization and suffix matching can serve a semantically inappropriate response; [src: docs/known-issues.md]
  they remain opt-in. Structured system/content blocks are not regex-normalized. [src: docs/known-issues.md]
- Oversized upstream responses stream to the primary client without retained replay; [src: docs/known-issues.md]
  coalesced waiters may need independent upstream requests. [src: docs/known-issues.md]
- Existing legacy cache files may retain permissive permissions. New files are private. [src: docs/known-issues.md]
- Native Windows process control and Linux/macOS service-manager activation are not [src: docs/known-issues.md]
  established by temporary-fixture tests on macOS. Reboots were not tested in this run. [src: docs/known-issues.md]
- Live API fidelity and performance were not remeasured. The historical technical [src: docs/known-issues.md]
  review is an archive, not evidence of current live behavior. [src: docs/known-issues.md]
- No dashboard, centralized remediation agent, generic operations runner or datastore [src: docs/known-issues.md]
  service is shipped. The operations inventory explicitly records these adaptations. [src: docs/known-issues.md]
